بالثناء على من خلقه وأطلق بالشكر مقوله لما قام أبدا بحق الله سبحانه، هذا سيد (1) الأولين والآخرين يقول: "لا أحصي ثناء عليك ) ، فمن أين يبقى للسان مجال لإرخاء العنان فبالحري(2). إذا قلت ما أذنبت قلت مجيبة وجودك ذنب لا يقاس به ذن فمن لم يأمن أن يناقش الحساب وآمن إن نوقش الحساب لحقه لا محالة العذاب، فكيف لا يكون صوفيا، قيل: الصوفي دمه هدر وملكـــه مباح. حكي عن معروف الكرخي أنه مر بإنسان تصدق بماء وهو يقول: رحم الله من يشرب. فأخذ معروف ذلك الماء وشرب، وقيل له: أليس كنت صائمًا؟ قال: بلى، ولكن منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين 293 قلت: دعوة مسلم لعلها تستجاب. وكان الصبيان يؤذون بهلولا ويرمونه بالأحجار، فجعل يقول لهم: ارموني بهذه الأحجار الصغار لئلا أحتاج إلى غسل الدم، فقيل له في ذلك، فأنشد(1): ليس للهارب في مهربــه أبــــدا مـن راحة إلا إليه لــــــي سى بأحجار الأذى لم أجد بـدا مـن العطف عليـه يطلع الله علـــــى فــرح القــوم فيـدنيني إليـــه ونحو هذا نقل الطرطوشي عن أويس، ويقول: تشغلوني بغسل الـدم عـن الصلاة. وقد تقدمت حكاية الذي سلب ثوبه فهتف بالسالب جعلتك في حل. فقل: قبلت؛ أن يلبس الثوب حلالا ولا يلبسه حرامًا. وعرف عياض بالبهلول بن راشد، وذكر من فضائله؛ أنه أخبر عن بعض أصحابه أنه ضرب بمقرعة بالليل فأتاه البهلول يسأله أن يجعل الذي فعل ذلك في ، حل، فقال الرجل: فعلوا بي، وفعلوا بي، وأجعلهم في حل؟ قال: أيسرك أن يحال بين أخيك المسلم وبين الجنة بسببك؟ فلم يزل بالرجل حتى جعل الجاني عليه في حل. وعرف أيضًا بعبد الجبار من الفقهاء المالكية ومن أكابر أصحاب سحنون، قال: كان يغدو إلى الجمعة إذا بشاب جميل حسن البزة يمشي في إثر صبية، فاتكأ عبد الجبار على نعله فقطع شسعه وناداه یا شاب فوقف يمشي إليه، وقال له: أنا شيخ ضعيف بصري، وانقطع شسعي، فأصلحه لي، فتناوله الشاب، ورأى عبـد الجبار الصبية تتباطأ في مشيها، فأصلحه، وأخذ منه النعل، ومشى في إثر الصبية، فقطعه ثانيًا، وناداه ليصلحه، فعطف عليه وقال: أنا قطعته يا شاب إشفاقًا على هذا الشاب من لفح النار، وبكى فبكى الفتى وجزاه خيرًا، وصحبه إلى الجامع، وحسنت توبته قال عياض وكان يتكلم بالحكمة، ومن حكمه: فلو أهمك شأنك لكل لسانك وتهيجت أحزانك.
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "newness" and "earnestness, seriousness, vigor" — the opposite of jest (hazl); also "good fortune" and "exertion of one's utmost effort."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the theological context, jidd denotes the total commitment of one's faculties to the worship of God, leaving no room for negligence or distraction — the very essence of sincerity (ikhlāṣ) in the spiritual path.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to the firmness of a rope or the solidity of ground; metaphorically, it signifies the soul's steadfastness in religious observance, unyielding against the pull of worldly concerns.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate emphasis (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — the station is defined by an equational structure, asserting a permanent state rather than a transient action.
translation:
I say — may God grant us success — the eighth station, which is the station of the elite among the scholars, is built upon the path of spiritual ascent (taraqqī). Whoever has not been enabled to cultivate all of his times [with worship], let him strive to cultivate the virtuous times [at least]. And it does not harm me what they have done, when God sets right what is mine. So let your intention, O brother in God, be that the first thing to which you direct your resolve is God, at the first moment of wakefulness from the night — and this is the first litany (wird). Then you return to sleep, so that it may be a foundation for rising at the last part of the night (sahar) — and this is the second litany. Then you rise at the last part of the night to complete what remains of your litany, or to recite the Qur'an until dawn breaks — and this is the third litany. With the rising of dawn, the fourth litany enters, extending until the prayer of illumination (ṣalāt al-ishrāq). Then the fifth litany enters, extending until the mid-morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā). Then the sixth litany extends until the sun's declination (zawāl), during which you take the midday nap (qaylūlah). Then the seventh litany extends until the completion of the noon prayer (ẓuhr). Then the eighth litany is that which lies between the two noons [i.e., ẓuhr and ʿaṣr]. Then the ninth litany extends until the yellowing of the sun. Then the tenth litany is when the sun has yellowed. Then the eleventh litany is between the two evening prayers [i.e., maghrib and ʿishāʾ]. Then the twelfth litany is after the night prayer (ʿatamah) until the first moment of wakefulness.

So it is incumbent upon you — if you cannot make your worship perpetual — to cultivate these times with litanies. Whenever you find a moment of leisure in any of them, you must seize it: either by occupying yourself with its specific litany, or with a private devotion (hajīr) that you have, or by making up what was strongly incumbent upon you that you missed in the preceding time. He said in *Bidāyat al-Hidāyah*: "It is incumbent that there be no neglected times, and that you assign to every time a specific occupation. For in this way the blessing of the times becomes manifest. For whoever leaves himself untended, neglected like the neglect of beasts, not knowing with what to occupy himself at each time — most of his times pass away wasted." End quote.

And consider, in the obligation of seclusion (iʿtikāf), the cultivation of times with acts of obedience — so it is incumbent that one intend this very intention in his seclusion. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī — may God have mercy on him — said: "A word I heard from al-Ḥajjāj upon the planks of this pulpit has struck me dead. I heard him say: 'A man whose hour of his life passes away in other than what he was created for — it is fitting that his regret extend over it until the Day of Resurrection.'" End quote.

There is no doubt that the truth is that a person should be, at every time, engaged in what is most fitting for that time. And it has preceded that this is the reality of the Sufi. And this is the ninth station.

---

**The Ninth Station: Taking Religion with Earnestness**

This is the station with which I began, and behold, I conclude with it — may God seal it for me with His grace and bounty. It is that a person be as was related in *al-Tanwīr*: "If it were said to him: 'Tomorrow you will die,' he would find nothing to add [to his deeds]." And in *al-Risālah*: Abū ʿAlī al-Thaqafī was speaking one day when ʿAbd Allāh ibn Munāzil said to him: "O Abū ʿAlī, prepare for death, for it is inevitable." So ʿAbd Allāh rested his arm [as a pillow], placed his head, and said: "I have already died." And Abū ʿAlī was cut short, because he could not respond with what [ʿAbd Allāh] had done — for Abū ʿAlī had attachments, while ʿAbd Allāh was detached, having no occupation.

Sufyān al-Thawrī — may God be pleased with him — said: "I saw in the mosque of Kūfah an old man saying: 'I have been in this mosque for thirty years waiting for death to descend upon me. If it came to me, I would not have been commanded anything, nor forbidden anything, nor would I have any claim against anyone, nor would anyone have any claim against me.'"

He said in *al-Iḥyāʾ*: "Every breath of your breaths is a final one, for it is possible that death is connected to it. And even if you suppose that death is not connected to it — is it not presented to you on the Day of Resurrection?"

A man said to Ibrāhīm ibn Adham: "How many obligatory acts are upon me in the day and night?" He said: "What is it to you to concern yourself with what you cannot fulfill? Upon you is what you know." The man pressed him repeatedly, so Ibrāhīm ibn Adham said to him: "Upon you, in every moment, are three necessary obligations — you disobey God if you abandon any one of them." He said: "What are they?" He said: "The remembrance of God, sincerity to Him, and contentment with everything that comes from God." End quote.

There is no doubt that the truth is this. For every breath that issues from a person is a vessel for a measure of God's decrees and a blessing from God. And the reality of gratitude (shukr) is the directing of the blessing toward obedience to the Benefactor.

He said in *al-Iḥyāʾ*: "In every breath that a person exhales and inhales, there are two blessings. For with its exhalation, the heart is relieved — and were it not to exit, the person would perish. And with the inhalation of the breath, the air-spirit gathers to the heart — and were its passage blocked, the heart would burn." And the day and night are twenty-four hours; in every hour there are nearly a thousand breaths, and every breath is nearly ten moments. And upon you in every moment are a thousand thousand blessings in every part of your parts.

Some of them said: "Consider the erectness of your stature, seeking by intention the height; and He made the two perforations of your ears connected to the brain, conveying what is delivered to them to the heart. He — glorified be He — placed in them the bitterness that prevents creeping creatures from reaching them, just as He placed saltiness in the two eyes to prevent them from melting. And He placed sweetness on the tongue, by which one tastes the sweet from the bitter. And He placed moisture in the two nostrils — were they dry, you would find no scent to smell. And He placed the two eyebrows above the eyes as a canopy protecting what descends from above."

These are all blessings whose gratitude you cannot enumerate — upon you in every one of these particulars, nay, in every part of the world, is to render their gratitude. For if you direct a single particular of your particulars toward other than the pleasure of your Lord, you have wronged all of the dominion (mulk) and the sovereignty (malakūt). Whoever opens his eyelid and directs it toward what is not lawful has disbelieved in every blessing of God upon him — God's blessings in the heavens and the earth and what is between them.

For God, in every blink, has two blessings in the eyelid itself. For God — glorified be He — created beneath every eyelid muscles, and for them tendons and ligaments connected to the nerves of the brain, by which the lowering of the upper eyelid and the raising of the lower eyelid are accomplished. And upon every eyelid are lashes. And God's blessing in their blackness is that it gathers the light of the eye — for whiteness disperses light, while blackness gathers it. And God's blessing in their arrangement in a single row is that it serves as a barrier preventing creeping creatures from crawling into the interior of the eye, and as a trap for the dust particles that scatter from the air. And God — in every single lash of them — has two blessings: in the softness of its base, and with the softness, the firmness of its erectness. And in the intertwining of the lashes, He has a blessing greater than all: for the dust of the air might prevent the opening of the eye, and were it to close completely, one would not see. So He gathered the eyelids to the extent that they intertwine with the lashes, and one sees from behind a lattice of hair. Thus the lattice of hair is a barrier preventing the entry of dust from outside, yet not preventing the extension of vision from inside.

And God — glorified and exalted be He — created the edges of the eyelids sharp, closing over the pupil like a polisher. For if dust strikes the pupil, the eyelids close once or twice, and the pupil is polished of the dust, and the particles exit to the corners of the eye. And since the fly has no eyelids, God created for it two hands — you see it perpetually wiping its two eyes with them to polish them of dust.

So whoever opens his eyelid where it is obligatory to lower it has disbelieved, by the opening of the eye, in God's blessing of the eyelids. And the eyelids do not stand except by the eye, nor the eye except by the head, nor the head except by the entire body, nor the body except by nourishment, nor nourishment except by water, earth, air, rain, clouds, sun, moon, and stars. And none of that stands except by the heavens, and the heavens by the angels. For all of it is like a single thing, parts of it connected to parts, like the connection of the limbs of the body to one another.

So if you have disbelieved in God — all of it, from the furthest reaches of the Pleiades to the earth's dust — there remains no angel, nor sphere, nor animal, nor plant, except that it curses you. And likewise, every limb, limb by limb — whenever you direct it toward other than what draws you near to God in proximity (zulfā) — even if you are spared from sin, you have exposed yourself through heedlessness to a loss and a regret that have no end. {«وَأَنذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ»} [Maryam: 39].

And from that is your hand — God has blessed you with it as a seizing instrument, extending toward things, comprising many joints so that it moves in directions, extending and bending toward you, not being like a fixed wooden post. Then He — glorified be He — made the head of the hand, creating the palm. Then He divided the head of the palm into five divisions — which are the fingers — and made them in two rows, such that the thumb is on one side and rotates around the remaining four.

And were the first and the last [of humanity] to gather to deduce, with fine reflection, another arrangement for the placement of the fingers other than that upon which they are placed — the distance of the thumb from the four, the variation of the four in length, and their arrangement in a single row — they would not be able to do so. For by this arrangement, grasping and giving are perfected. For if one spreads them, they are a plate upon which one places what he wishes; if one gathers them, they are an instrument for striking; if one closes them incompletely, they are a ladle for him; if one spreads them and closes the fingers, they are a shovel for him.

Then He — glorified be He — created the nails as an adornment for the fingertips, or for picking up fine objects that the fingertips cannot grasp, and for scratching the body with them. For the nail is the most lowly of the limbs — yet were a person to lack it and an itch were to appear on him, he would be the most incapable and weakest of creation, and no one would stand in his place in scratching his body. Then He guided the two hands to the places of itching, so that they extend to them even in sleep. And were one to seek help from another, he would not find the place of the itch except after great exertion.

Then He prepared for him an instrument by which to take nourishment. Then suppose you have taken food with your hand — from where does this suffice you until it reaches the stomach? So He — glorified be He — made the mouth a passage to the stomach, and then what is in it of wisdoms beyond merely being a passage. For when you place food in the mouth as a single piece, its swallowing is not facilitated — so it needs a mill to grind the food. So He — glorified be He — created two jaws from two bones, and set in them the teeth, and matched the molars of the upper upon the lower, to grind the food with them thoroughly.

Then the food sometimes needs breaking, sometimes needs cutting, and then needs grinding after that. So He divided the teeth into grinders — which are the molars — and into sharp incisors like the canine teeth, and into what is suitable for breaking like the fangs. Then He made the joint of the two jaws loose, such that the lower jaw advances and retreats, rotating upon the upper jaw like the rotation of a millstone. And were it not for this, nothing would be facilitated except the striking of one upon the other, and grinding would not be accomplished by that. So He made the lower jaw move with a rotational motion, and the upper jaw fixed, not moving.

Then suppose you have placed the food in the cavity of the mouth — how does the food move to beneath the teeth? And how do the teeth draw it to themselves? Or how is it managed by the hand inside the mouth? So God blessed you by creating the tongue, which roams the sides of the mouth and returns the food from the middle to the teeth — this, along with what is in the tongue of the benefit of taste, and what God created in it of a spring from which saliva flows, pouring forth in the measure of need, to moisten the food with it. For a person cannot swallow except that it slides down with saliva. And He subjugated it for this matter, such that you see food from afar, and it [the saliva] stirs to service before the food reaches it.

Then you find these blessings in the tongue to be slight in comparison to the great benefit — which is the power of speech (manṭiq). For the tongue is among God's great blessings and the wonders of His strange craftsmanship. Were it to have no motion except in praising Him who created it, and in releasing its utterance in gratitude, it would never fulfill God's right — glorified be He. This is the master of the first and the last [i.e., the Prophet ﷺ] saying: "I cannot enumerate praise of You." So from where does there remain for the tongue any field for releasing its reins?

It is fitting, then, if you say "I have not sinned," that I say in response: "Your very existence is a sin that no sin can be measured against." So whoever does not feel safe from being scrutinized in the reckoning, yet feels safe — if he is scrutinized in the reckoning, punishment will inevitably befall him. So how could he not be a Sufi? It is said: "The Sufi — his blood is shed with impunity, and his property is forfeit."

It is related of Maʿrūf al-Karkhī that he passed by a man who was giving water in charity, saying: "May God have mercy on whoever drinks." So Maʿrūf took that water and drank. And it was said to him: "Were you not fasting?" He said: "Yes, but I said: 'A Muslim's supplication — perhaps it will be answered.'"

And the boys used to harm Buhlūl and throw stones at him. So he began saying to them: "Throw at me these small stones, lest I need to wash off blood." So it was said to him about that, and he recited:

"There is for the fugitive, in his fleeing, never any rest except toward Him. I have found no alternative but to turn with affection toward the stones of harm. God sees the joy of the people and draws me near to Him."

And similar to this, al-Ṭarṭūshī transmitted from Uways, who said: "You occupy me with washing off blood from the prayer." And the story has preceded of the one whose garment was stripped from him, and he called out to the stripper: "I have made you free of it." So say: "I accept — that he wear the garment lawfully, and not wear it unlawfully."

And ʿIyāḍ identified him as Buhlūl ibn Rāshid, and mentioned of his virtues that he was informed about one of his companions that he was struck with a whip at night. So Buhlūl came to him asking him to make the one who did that free of blame. The man said: "They did to me, and they did to me — and I should make them free of blame?" He said: "Would it please you that your Muslim brother be barred from Paradise because of you?" And he kept at the man until he made the one who wronged him free of blame.

And ʿIyāḍ also identified ʿAbd al-Jabbār, one of the Mālikī jurists and among the greatest companions of Saḥnūn. He said: "He was going out to the Friday [prayer] when a handsome young man, well-dressed, was walking in pursuit of a young woman. So ʿAbd al-Jabbār leaned on his sandal and cut its strap, and called out: 'O young man!' So he stopped and walked toward him. He said to him: 'I am a weak old man, failing of sight, and my sandal strap has broken — so fix it for me.' So the young man took it, and ʿAbd al-Jabbār saw the young woman slowing in her walk. So he fixed it, took the sandal from him, and walked in pursuit of the young woman. Then he cut it a second time, and called him to fix it. So he turned to him and said: 'I cut it, O young man, out of compassion for this young man from the scorching of the Fire.' And he wept, and the young man wept, and thanked him well, and accompanied him to the mosque, and his repentance became good."

ʿIyāḍ said: "And he used to speak with wisdom." And among his wise sayings: "Were your own affair to concern you, your tongue would be restrained, and your sorrows would be stirred."

title_en: The Ninth Station: Taking Religion with Earnestness — The Virtue of Overlooking Offenses and Upholding the Rights of Muslims
arabic_text: 294 منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين وعرف أيضًا بزيد بن بشير، قال: كان فقيها ثقة سمع من ابن القاسم وابن وهب وأشهب. قال: من فضائله أن طريقه إلى الجامع كان على الخرازين، فأقبل يومًا مع الطلبة إذا بشاب من الخرازين قام على دكانه، وقال لجاره: قم الق التيس ما رأيت أوحش من هذا الشيخ فنكس زيد رأسه، فلما انصرف من الجامع عاوده الفتى بقبيح ، فلم يلتفت إليه زيد وهم طلبته بضرب الفتى، فبلغ ذلك زيدًا، فسألهم عنه، فقالوا: هو ما قيل أصلحك الله لاستخفافه بحقك، فقال لهم: أعطي الله عهدًا لئن تقدم إليه أحد الأقصينه ولا وطئ لي بساطا، أنا أصلح شأنه، وصر في صرة عشرة دراهم، وجعلها في جيبه، واستعمل لفرد نعل قبالًا واهيا، توجه إلى الجامع، فلما مر بالشاب قام لعادته وتكلم بقبيح قوله، فلما حاذاه الشيخ اتكأ على نعله فقطع القبال، ثم مال إلى الشاب فسلم عليه وقال: أي بني لعل عندك قبالًا؟ فأدخل زيد يده وأخرج الصرة من جيبه ودفعها له، فقال الشاب: ما هذا؟ فقال: صنعت لنا قبالًا فكافأناك. فسار إلى الجامع، فلما كان انصرافه منه، ومر بالشاب قام على قدميه، وقال: الحمد لله الذي خص بلدنا بهذا الشيخ الفاضل، اللهم أبقه لنا، واحرزه على المسلمين. وقد تقدم قبل هذا بيسير مقام السبائي من العلماء المالكية ودينه وفضله، نقل عنه عياض: أنه مر بموضع فإذا بشيخ لم ير أجمل منه لحية وهو يزمر ببوق، فقال السبائي لبعض أصحابه لعلك قالت لك نفسك: إنك خير منه إنه مسلم، والله ما أرى لي فضلا على أهل الكبائر من المسلمين، فإذا رأيتم أهل البلاء فاحمدوا الله على العافية، فذكر أن الرجل ريء بأثر ذلك وقد تاب وحج وحسنت حاله. ولقي سکران بشر الحافي وقال له يا سيدي يا أبا ،نصر، فلم يدفعه بشر عن نفسه، فلما تولى تغرغرت عينا بشر ، وقال رجل أحب رجلًا على خير توهمه، لعل المحب قد نجا والمحبوب لا يدري ما حاله. وعرف عياض أيضًا بأبي محرز ، وذكر من دينه وفضله قال: أطلع الناس على ماله يوم ولي القضاء، أشهدهم إن ظهرت زيادة على ما رأوا فهو خائن. قال: وقف عليه رجل به نبيذ فكثر من الكلام، فأمر به أبو محرز إلى السجن، فقال الرجل: أيها القاضي، إن زوجي مهرها ثلاثمائة دينار وهي طالق إن لم تغن لي، فالتفت أبو محرز إلى جلسائه وقال: أرأيتم ما حل بنا من هذا؟ ثم سكت ساعة وقال: "أتيناكم منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين 295 أتيناكم فحيونا نحييكم، ولولا الحبة الصفراء لم تسمن عذاريكم، ولولا الذهب ، (1) الإبريز لم نحلل “بواديكم ، وقد تقدم في المقام الثالث أن الغضب على الجاني إنما هو بقدر غضب الله عليه فنقيم عليه الحد بلا زيادة سوط واحد، ونراعي له حق الإسلام فلا نشوش عليه أمر دنياه، وقد قال رسول الله ﷺ للذي سب الذي أقام عليه الحد:”لا تكونوا عونا للشيطان على أخيكم؛ إنه يحب الله ورسوله"(2). وانظر قضية عمر رضي الله عنه حين كف عن السكران قائلا: لا أحب أن أضرب مسلمًا حمية لنفسي، وقضيته مع الذين اطلع عليهم وهم شرب، وقضية الله عنه إذ قال: الحمد لله الذي لم يفضحهم على يدي، وأعتق رقبة عثمان رضي شكرا الله تعالى أن لا يكون جرت على يديه فضيحة رجل مسلم. وعرف عياض أيضًا بأبي العباس التميمي، قال: كان حافظا للمسائل من أهل الاجتهاد والورع قرئ عليه بالقيروان وسمع منه قال واجتمع الناس على فضله. كانوا جالسين معه يومًا على باب داره إذ وثب فقال لهم: قوموا فادخلوا، فدخلوا وأغلق الباب ولا يدرون ما السبب، وأقبل ينظر من شق الباب ثم فتح الباب، وقال لهم: اخرجوا، فسألوه: ما السبب؟ فقال: رأيت سكرانًا فلم أرد أن تروه، فقالوا له: من هو؟ فقال: أنا سترته منكم، ثم أخبركم به! مع علمه من وعرف أيضًا بالقاضي ابن السليم قال: كان حافظا للفقه، وكان أهل الزهد والبر، طال هربه من السلطان إلى أن أنشبه المقدار، فنال رياسة الدنيا والدين بالأندلس، فما استحال عن هديه ولا غرته الدنيا بوجه. حضر يومًا مسجدًا بأطراف قرطبة لانتظار جنازة، فحان وقت الصلاة فلم يؤذن هناك، فقال لرجل من العامة : يا هذا اخرج فأذن فإذا به جاهل فتغير لقوله، وقال له: لم تر في المجلس أنحس مني؟ فتبسم القاضي واستغفر وخرج بنفسه، فأذن ورجع فصلى بالناس، ثم قال للرجل: وجدت أنحس منك، فلا تعد لمثل قولك، ولكن قل: لا أحسن تاب الله علينا وعليك.
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Earnestness, seriousness, exertion in a matter; the opposite of jest (hazl). Also denotes newness (jadīd) and cutting (jadd) — the severing of laxity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, jidd signifies the soul's total commitment to divine commands, stripping away worldly pretexts; it is the engine of maqāmāt (stations).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — firm resolve in action; metaphorical (majāz) — the "cutting off" of base desires as one cuts a strap (qibāl).
- Root: س-ت-ر (s-t-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal, shield; satara means veiling a fault from sight.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine covering (satr) of sins is a sign of divine mercy; human covering of a brother's fault mirrors this attribute.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical covering; metaphorical — concealing moral defects, as in the Prophet's command not to aid Satan against a brother.
- Root: غ-ض-ب (gh-d-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Anger, wrath; intense displeasure rising in the breast.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine anger (ghaḍab) is His will to punish; human anger must be proportioned to divine anger — no excess beyond the prescribed ḥadd.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — emotional rage; metaphorical — judicial severity executed without personal spite, as in ʿUmar's restraint.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When a noun follows another without a conjunction to clarify it (e.g., "زيد بن بشير" — Zayd, son of Bashīr), the second term restricts the first, demanding precise identification of the subject before any predicate is attached.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you to the path of the rightly guided, and grant us steadfastness in the stations of the sincere:

294 — The Method of Ascent — The Ninth Station: Taking Religion with Earnestness.

Know that this station is also known through the account of Zayd ibn Bashīr. He was a jurist of trustworthiness, having heard from Ibn al-Qāsim, Ibn Wahb, and Ashab. Among his virtues is this: his path to the congregational mosque passed through the street of the shoemakers (al-kharrāzīn). One day, as he approached with the students, a young man among the shoemakers stood upon his stall and said to his neighbor: "Rise, go meet that billy-goat — I have never seen anything more hideous than this shaykh!" Zayd lowered his head. When he departed from the mosque, the youth accosted him again with foul speech, but Zayd paid him no heed. His students, however, intended to strike the youth. When this reached Zayd, he asked them about him, and they said: "He is the one who said, may Allah set you right, what was said — for his contempt of your right." So Zayd said to them: "I have made a covenant with Allah that if any of you advances toward him, I will expel him, and he shall never tread my carpet. I myself will set his affair aright." Then he wrapped ten dirhams in a cloth bundle, placed it in his pocket, and fitted a worn-out strap (qibāl) to the sole of his sandal. He set out for the mosque. When he passed by the youth, the young man rose as was his habit and spoke his foul words. When the shaykh drew alongside him, he leaned upon his sandal and snapped the strap. Then he turned to the youth, greeted him with peace, and said: "My son, perhaps you have a strap with you?" Zayd then put his hand in his pocket, drew out the bundle, and handed it to him. The youth said: "What is this?" He replied: "You made a strap for us, so we have recompensed you." Then he proceeded to the mosque. When he was returning from it and passed by the youth, the young man stood upon his feet and said: "Praise be to Allah who has singled out our land for this virtuous shaykh! O Allah, preserve him for us, and guard him for the Muslims!"

And shortly before this, there has preceded the station of al-Sabā'ī among the Mālikī scholars, his religion and his virtue. ʿIyāḍ transmitted from him: He passed by a place and saw an old man, the most beautiful of men in beard, who was blowing a horn. Al-Sabā'ī said to one of his companions: "Perhaps your soul has said to you: 'You are better than him, for he is a Muslim.' By Allah, I do not see any merit for myself over the people of grave sins among the Muslims. So when you see people of affliction, praise Allah for well-being." He mentioned that the man was seen after that — he had repented, performed the pilgrimage, and his state had become good.

And he (al-Sabā'ī) met a drunkard, and Bishr al-Ḥāfī said to him: "O my master, O Abā Naṣr!" And Bishr did not push him away from himself. When he turned away, Bishr's eyes brimmed with tears, and he said: "A man loved another man for a good he imagined in him — perhaps the lover has been saved, while the beloved does not know his own state."

And ʿIyāḍ also transmitted about Abū Muḥriz, mentioning his religion and virtue. He said: He showed his wealth to the people on the day he was appointed to the judgeship, and made them witness: "If any increase appears beyond what you have seen, then I am a traitor." He said: A man with a case of wine stood before him and spoke at length. Abū Muḥriz ordered him to prison. The man said: "O judge, my wife's dowry is three hundred dīnārs, and she is divorced if she does not sing for me!" Abū Muḥriz turned to his companions and said: "Do you see what has befallen us from this man?" Then he was silent for a moment and said: "We have come to you — so greet us, and we greet you. Were it not for the yellow grain, your cheeks would not have fattened; and were it not for refined gold, we would not have settled your valleys."

And it has preceded in the Third Station that anger against the offender is only to the measure of Allah's anger against him — so we establish the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) upon him without adding a single lash, and we observe for him the right of Islam, so we do not disturb his worldly affair. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the one who cursed the man upon whom the ḥadd had been established: "Do not be helpers of Satan against your brother; verily, he loves Allah and His Messenger." {«لَا تَكُونُوا عَوْنًا لِلشَّيْطَانِ عَلَى أَخِيكُمْ؛ إِنَّهُ يُحِبُّ اللهَ وَرَسُولَهُ»}

And consider the case of ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — when he refrained from striking the drunkard, saying: "I do not love to strike a Muslim out of personal zeal." And his case with those whom he came upon while they were drinking, and his saying — may Allah be pleased with him — "Praise be to Allah who did not expose them at my hands," and he freed the neck of ʿUthmān — may Allah be pleased with him — in gratitude to Allah that no disgrace of a Muslim man had been carried out at his hands.

And ʿIyāḍ also transmitted about Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Tamīmī. He said: He was a preserver of legal cases, among the people of independent judgment (ijtihād) and scrupulous piety (waraʿ). He was read to in Qayrawān, and he was heard from. He said: And the people agreed upon his virtue. They were sitting with him one day at the door of his house, when he leapt up and said to them: "Rise, enter!" So they entered, and he closed the door, and they did not know the reason. He began looking through the crack of the door, then opened it and said: "Go out." They asked him: "What is the reason?" He said: "I saw a drunkard, and I did not want you to see him." They said to him: "Who is he?" He said: "I concealed him from you, then I would tell you of him!" — despite his knowledge of him.

And he is also known as the Judge Ibn al-Salīm. He said: He was a preserver of jurisprudence, and he was among the people of asceticism (zuhd) and piety. His flight from the Sultan was prolonged until destiny ensnared him, and he attained the leadership of this world and religion in al-Andalus. Yet he did not change from his guidance, nor did this world beguile him in any way. One day he attended a mosque on the outskirts of Cordoba to await a funeral. The time of prayer came, and no one gave the call to prayer there. He said to a man of the common folk: "O you, go out and give the call." And behold, he was an ignorant man, and he became angry at his words and said to him: "Did you not see in the assembly anyone more ill-omened than me?" The judge smiled, sought forgiveness, and went out himself. He gave the call, returned, and led the people in prayer. Then he said to the man: "I have found someone more ill-omened than you. Do not repeat such a saying, but say: 'I do not know how — Allah has turned in mercy upon us and upon you.'"

title_en: The Ninth Station: Taking Religion with Earnestness (al-Akhdh bi al-Jidd fī al-Dīn)
arabic_text: 296 منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين وعرف عياض بعبد الرحمن بن مدارك، قال: كان عالمًا بمذهب مالك، حافظًا له، راسخًا في علمه، ورعًا كثير التهجد، مات بعض أصحابه وترك ولدًا فسأل عنه فأخبر سلوكه غير القوام، فأمر أن يؤتى به، فشاهد عنده المجلس وحـان وقـت الصلاة فقدمه صلي بالناس، فلما فرغوا وخلا به ،وعظه وقال له: انظر، لا تجعل الناس يقولون: انظر من قدم عبد الرحمان يصلي به. ومن التحبير أن بعض المشائخ اجتمع عنده مال لعمارة بعض الرباطات، : فعرفه قوم من اللصوص، فتشبهوا بزي الصالحين، وأخفوا سلاحهم، واستضافوه، فلما قدم إليهم الطعام وغسلوا أيديهم، وكانت له ابنة زمنة، فشربت من ذلك الماء، واستعملت منه تبركًا للضيفان فشفاها الله في الوقت فجاء الشيخ، وألطف بهم، وقال: إنكم مباركون، وقص عليهم القصة، فوقع عليهم الندم، وقالوا له: إنا لغير هذا حضرنا، ولكن بعد ما أحسن الله بنا هذا الإحسان وأسبل علينا هذا الستر فقد تبنا. وفي الرسالة: ليست الفتوة أن تحسن إلى من أحسن إليك، فإن ذلك جزاء ومكافأة، ولكن الفتوة أن تحسن إلى من أساء إليك. قالوا: الصوفي كالأرض؛ يطرح عليها كل قبيح، ولا يبرز منها إلا كل مليح حكي أن بعض الصوفية كان ترقيه بصراح الشكر، فزاره رجل قطعت بالفور يده فقال زورة بقطع يد، قال: يا سيدي، ما تسببت؟ قال: على هذا أطالبك لم تحاج صاحبك ولم تتركه يقتص منه. اهـ. وتسمى الصوفية هذا القلب يستغفر لظالمه حتى ينقلب، كمـا تقـدم فـي اللصوص الذين قالوا: لغير هذا جئنا، جاؤوا للعصيان بقلوب قاسية، فنالوا بركة المتاب وإصلاح الطوية. والشيء يذكر بالشيء؛ من الرسالة عن الزجاجي قال ماتت أمي فورثت دارًا بعتها بخمسين دينارًا، وخرجت إلى الحج، فلما بلغت بابل استقبلني واحد من القياقنة وقال: إيش معك؟ فقلت في نفسي الصدق خير، فقلت: خمسون دينارا، فقال: ناولنيها، فناولته الصرة، فعدها، فإذا هي خمسون، فقال لي: خذها، فلقد أخذني صدقك، ثم نزل من الدابة وقال اركبها فقلت لا أريد ولا بد، فألح فركبتها فقال: وأنا على أثرك، فلما كان العام المستقبل لحقني ولازمني حتى مات. وقد تقدم في آخر المقام الثاني قول تاج الدين حظ النفس في المعصية ظاهر منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين 297 جلي، وحظها في الطاعة باطن خفي، فراجعه. ومن نحو هذا قول السبائي: ما أرى لي فضلا على أهل الكبائر، حكاية حسان بن أبي سنان لقي رجلًا به زهد وكان مع حسان رجل، فسأله حسان مسألة لطيفة فقال الرجل: تسائل هذا مثل هذه المساءلة، حتى يظن في نفسه أنه شيء؟ فقال له: وما يدريك لعله تكون فيه خصلة يحبها الله وفيك خصلة يبغضها الله فقال له: يا عبد الله وما هذه الخصلة التي فيه يحبها الله، والخصلة التي فيه يبغضها الله؟ قال له: لعله حين رآك حدثته نفسه أنك خير منه، ولعلك حين رأيته حدثتك نفسك أنك خير منه. وقد تقدم في آخر المقام الثاني في محاجة معاوية للمسور؛ إذ قال له: ألم يكن لك يا مسور ذنوب تخاف أن يؤاخذك الله بها؟ فقال: بلى، فقال: وما جعلك أحق أن ترجو المغفرة مني وإني وإياك على دين يقبل الله فيه الحسنات إلى آخر الحكاية، حتى قال المسور: فعرفت أنـه فكان بعد لا يذكره إلا بخير. وفي الكتب المنزلة حذر الصديقين أني إن وضعت عدلي عليهم عذبتهم. وعن حفص بن حميد قال: قلت لابن المبارك رأيت رجلًا قتل رجلًا، فوقع في نفسي إني أفضل منه، فقال لي ابن المبارك: أمنك على نفسك أشد وانظر إذا كان متقي الشرك يوشك أن يغفر له، فكيف لا يترك به من يوقن خصمني، (1) من ذنبه. اهـ. أنه إن نوقش الحساب عذب، فقد صح من نوقش الحساب عذب). وثبت القرآن نفسك " (2) إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ، وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ ﴾ [النساء: 48]. اهـ. عاد الكلام إلى سيد الأنام : لا أحصي ثناء عليك، أنت كما أثنيت على ، فكيف بمن دونه ؟ فبالحري لمن رأى المنة وأيقن بالتقصير أن تصدر منه الحالة التي هي ثمرتها، وذلك الاستحياء حق الحياء، وهذه حالة الرجل الذي غبطه الحسن البصري رضي الله عنه، وذلك أنه قيل له: هاهنا رجل لم نره قط إلا جالسًا وحده خلف سارية، فقال الحسن: إذا رأيتموه فأخبروني، فنظروا إليه ذات 298 منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين يوم، فقالوا للحسن هذا الرجل الذي أخبرناك به فمشى إليه الحسن، وقال: يا عبد الله، ما يمنعك من مجالسة الناس؟ فقال: أمر شغلني عن الناس، فما يمنعك أن تأتي هذا الرجل الذي يقال له الحسن فتجلس إليه؟ فقال: أمر شغلني عن الحسن وعن الناس، فقال الحسن: وما ذاك الشغل يرحمك الله؟ فقال: إني أصبح وأمسي بين ذنب ونعمة، فرأيت أن أشغل نفسي بالاستغفار لذنبي والشكر على نعم ربي، فقال له الحسن يا عبد الله أنت أفقه عندي من الحسن فالزم ما أنت عليه. اهـ. ولا شك أن هذا هو حقيقة الحياء لم يبق له تشوق لحظ ولا بقاء مع نفس. قال تاج الدين في حكمه مطلب العارفين من الله الصدق بالعبودية والقيام بحق الربوبية. قال شارحها من غير طلب لحظ ولا بقاء مع نفس، ويتبين بها مصداق قول ابن العربي في سراجه كان الطرطوشي يقول لنا هل لكم في أن نخرج بأنفسنا ونتبتل إلى ربنا ؟ قال ابن العربي: فكنت أقول له: إذا حصلت ما أؤمل من العلم كنت لك صاحبًا في هذا الغرض، والذي ظهر لي أن شيخنا أبا بكر رضي الله عنه لم تكن له عزيمة على هذه القصة فإن من أرادها لم يحتج فيها إلى صاحب إلا الذي تبتل له. اهـ نصه رحمه الله وانظر ، يشهد لهذا ما حكاه في الرسالة عن بعض المشائخ قال: كنت في البادية وحدي فضاق صدري فقلت: يا إنس كلموني، يا جن، هاتف أيش تريد؟ فقلت: أريد الله فقال له الهاتف: حتى تريد الله. اهـ. وتبين أن هذه كلها حظوظ وبقايا مع النفوس، ومن استحيا من الله حق الحياء فهتف بي غاب عن الأغيار. والشيء يذكر بالشيء؛ حكى في الرسالة أيضًا عن بعضهم أنه قيل له: ادع لي، الأجنبية أن تجعل بينك وبين مولاك واسطة. قال: كفاك من وقال بكر بن عبد الله يا ابن آدم إذا شئت أن تدخل على مولاك بغير إذن دخلت عليه، قيل: وكيف ذلك؟ قال: تسبغ وضوءك وتدخل محرابك، فإذا أنت قد دخلت على مولاك بغير إذن وتكلمه بغير ترجمان. ونقل الآجري عن وهب بن منبه: أن راهبًا تخلى في صومعته زمان عيسى عليه السلام فأراده إبليس، فلم يقدر عليه ، ثم أتاه بكل زائرة وقال له: افتح؛ فإني إن ذهبت ندمت، فلم يقدر عليه، فأتاه متشبها بالمسيح ابن مريم، وناداه: أيها الراهب، منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين 299 أشرف عليَّ أكلمك، فقال: انطلق إلى شأنك، فلست أرد ما مضى من عمري، فقال: فأشرف عليَّ، فأنا المسيح، فقال: وإن كنت المسيح فما لي إليك حاجة، أليس قد أمرتنا بالعبادة وواعدتنا القيامة، فلو جئتني اليوم بغير ذلك لم أقبله منك، انطلق الله لشأنك، فلا حاجة لي فيك، فانطلق اللعين وتركه. يقولون رضي عنهم جميع الأغيار والأنوار والأحوال والدنيا والآخرة والنعم الظاهرة والباطنة لا تلاحظ شيئًا ذلك، ولا تركنن إليه، ولا تعتمد عليه بقي أو ذهب فإن ذلك قادح في إخلاص من التوحيد. وفي الإشارات: لا تركنن لشيء دوننا إن أويت إلى العمل رددناه عليك، وإن وثقت بالحال وقفناك معه، وإن أنست بالوجد استدرجناك فيه، وإن لحظت الخلق وكلناك إليهم، وإن اعتززت بالمعرفة نكرناها عليك فأي حيلة لك، وأي قوة معك، فارضنا لك ربَّاً حتى نرضاك لنا عبدا. ونقل عياض في مداركه عن ابن المبارك قال: مررت بحائك وقد انقطع شسع نعلي فلقيني بقبال فقلت: أللثواب فعلتها؟ قال: نعم، فكنت إذا جزت به ملت إليه فسلمت عليه، ثم افتقدته فأصبته قد أغلق حانوته، فسألت عنه بعض جيرانه، فقلت: إن كان مريضًا عدناه أو مشغولا أعناه أو فقيرًا واسيناه، فقالوا: لا علم لنا به فاستدللت على منزله فخرج إلي فسألته: ما شغلك عن حانوتك؟ فقال لي: أنت يا ابن المبارك يراك الناس تميل إلي، فألبستني قميصا ليس علي منه شيء فأخذت بكمه فسرت به إلى المقابر، فقلت: هذا قبر فلان، كان شأنه كذا من وكذا، وهذا قبر فلان كان من شأنه كذا وكذا. فقال: يا ابن المبارك، لا أعرف ما تقول ليس الرجل كل الرجل من وصفته الألسن، وليس الرجل كل الرجل من رمقته الأعين، إنما الرجل من ستر الله عليـه فـي حياتـه فأدخله قبـره مستورًا، ثم أبرزه يوم القيامة ليس عليه ذلة من معصية، فذلك الرجل. وقال في الرسالة ومنهم؛ يعني من مشائخ الصوفية رويم بن من جلة المشائخ، سأله رجل وقال له: أوصني؟ فقال: ما هذا الأمر إلا بذل الروح، فإن أمكنك الدخول مع هذا وإلا فلا تشتغل بترهات الصوفية. اهـ. أحمد بغدادي 09 وقد قال سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ الله :[الذاريات: 56] والعبادة بذل المجهود في مرضات المعبود من غير طلب لحظ 300 منهج الترقي المقام التاسع: الأخذ بالجد في الدين ولا بقاء مع نفس. قال تاج الدين في حكمه كيف تطلب العوض على عمل هو متصدق به عليك، أم كيف تطلب الجزاء على صدق هو مهديه إليك؟ قال الواسطي: مطالبة الأعواض على الطاعات من نسيان الفضل. وقال تاج الدين أيضًا في حكمه: المؤمن يشغله الثناء على الله عن أن يكون لنفسه شاكرًا، وتشغله حقوق الله عن أن يكون لحظوظه ذاكرًا. وقال أيضًا في حكمه لولا جميل ستره لم يكن عمل أهلًا للقبول. وقال أيضًا في حكمه أنت إلى حلمه إذا أطعته أحوج منك إلى حلمه إذا عصيته، يقول الصادق المصدوق : “لن يدخل أحدكم الجنة عمله”، قالوا: ولا أنت يا رسول الله؟ قال: ولا أنا، إلا أن يتغمدني الله منه برحمة(1)، وفي الصحيح: يقول : “أنا أخشاكم الله”، قال الله عز وجل: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَوا [فاطر: 28]، قال في الإحياء: عليك إن كنت من المرابطين المراقبين لنفسك أن تطالع أحوال الرجال والنساء من المتعبدين لينبعث نشاطك ويتوفر حرصك، وإياك أن تنظر إلى أهل عصرك ، فإنك إن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك، ومن أحسن علاج النفس صحبة مجتهد في العبادة، قال بعضهم: كنت إذا اعترتني فترة نظرت نظرة فعملت عليها أسبوعًا إلى محمد بن واسع وإلى اجتهاده، وقد كان إمامنا مالك يأتي محمد بن المنكدر ، وكان أحمد بن حنبل ويحيى بن معين يختلفان إلى معروف الكرخي، ولم يكن في علم الظاهر بمنزلتهما. وكان الإمام الشافعي يجلس بين يدي شيبان الراعي كما يقعد الصبي في المكتب. قال في الإحياء إلا أن هذا قد تعذر، فينبغي أن يرجع إلى سماع أحوالهم ومطالعة أخبارهم وما كانوا فيه من الجهد الجهيد، وقد انقضى تعبهم، وبقي ثوابهم ونعيمهم. دخل قوم لزيارة عمر بن عبد العزيز وفيهم شاب نحيل الجسم فقال له عمر: یا فتى ما الذي بلغ بك ما أرى؟ فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، أسقام وأمراض، فقال: سألتك بالله إلا صدقتني فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين ذقت حلاوة الدنيا فوجدتها مرة، فصغر في عيني زهرتها ونضارتها واستوى عندي ذهبها وحجرها، وكأني أنظر إلى
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Earnestness, seriousness, exertion of effort; the opposite of jest (hazl); also "newness" (jiddah) — here connoting fresh, vigorous resolve in religious practice.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The quality of unwavering commitment in worship and moral conduct, aligning the soul's intention with divine command without laxity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is firmness in a matter; metaphorically, it denotes the soul's total investment in the path of God, stripping away pretense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) — e.g., "fa-lammā faraghū wa-khalā bihi" (when they finished and he was alone with him) — governing temporal sequence and narrative flow.
translation:
I say — may God guide us and you to the path of the rightly guided and grant us success in following the conduct of the best of creation, our master Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Know that the ninth station on the path of ascent is the taking of religion with earnestness and the abandonment of negligence in the stations of the religion. This is the station of those who have realized the truth of servitude and have severed their attachment to whims and worldly portions.

ʿIyāḍ related, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mudārik, that he was a scholar of the school of Mālik, a preserver of it, deeply rooted in his knowledge, scrupulously pious, and frequent in night prayer. One of his companions died, leaving a young son. He asked about him and was told that his conduct was not upright. So he ordered that the boy be brought to him. When the boy came, he witnessed the gathering at his place, and when the time of prayer arrived, he put him forward to lead the people in prayer. When they finished and he was alone with him, he admonished him and said: "Look — do not let people say: 'See whom ʿAbd al-Raḥmān put forward to lead the prayer!'"

And from al-Taḥbīr: Some of the shaykhs had money gathered with him for the construction of certain ribāṭs (spiritual retreats). A group of thieves learned of this, so they disguised themselves in the garb of the righteous, hid their weapons, and sought his hospitality. When food was set before them and they washed their hands, he had a daughter who was paralyzed (zamina). She drank from that water and used it seeking blessing (tabarrukan) from the guests, and God cured her instantly. The shaykh came and treated them kindly, saying: "You are blessed," and recounted the story to them. Remorse fell upon them, and they said: "We did not come for this, but after God has bestowed this favor upon us and cast this veil of concealment over us, we have repented."

And in al-Risālah: "Chivalry (futūwah) is not that you do good to one who has done good to you, for that is recompense and requital. Rather, chivalry is that you do good to one who has done evil to you." They said: "The Sufi is like the earth — every ugly thing is cast upon it, and nothing emerges from it but every beautiful thing."

It is related that one of the Sufis was advancing in rank through the sincerity of his gratitude (ṣirāḥ al-shukr). A man visited him whose hand had been cut off instantly. He said: "A visit with a severed hand!" The Sufi said: "O my master, what was the cause?" He replied: "On this I hold you accountable — why did you not argue on behalf of your companion and leave him to exact retribution from him?" End quote.

The Sufis call this heart that seeks forgiveness for its oppressor until he turns — as mentioned previously in the story of the thieves who said: "We did not come for this." They came for disobedience with hard hearts, yet they attained the blessing of repentance and the rectification of intention.

And one thing recalls another. From al-Risālah, on the authority of al-Zajjājī, he said: "My mother died, and I inherited a house which I sold for fifty dīnārs, and I set out for the Pilgrimage. When I reached Bābil, one of the Qayāqinah met me and said: 'What do you have with you?' I said to myself: 'Truthfulness is better.' So I said: 'Fifty dīnārs.' He said: 'Hand them to me.' So I handed him the purse. He counted them, and they were fifty. He said to me: 'Take them — your truthfulness has seized me.' Then he dismounted from his beast and said: 'Ride it.' I said: 'I do not wish to.' But he insisted, so I rode it. He said: 'And I am following your tracks.' When the next year came, he caught up with me and stayed with me until he died."

And it has preceded at the end of the second station the saying of Tāj al-Dīn: "The soul's share in disobedience is apparent and clear, while its share in obedience is hidden and subtle — so review it."

And of similar import is the saying of al-Sibāʿī: "I do not see any merit for myself over the people of major sins."

The story of Ḥassān ibn Abī Sinān: He met a man who had asceticism (zuhd) with him, and there was a man with Ḥassān. Ḥassān asked the ascetic a subtle question, and the man said: "Do you ask someone like this such a question, until he thinks of himself as something?" Ḥassān said to him: "What makes you know? Perhaps he has a trait that God loves, and you have a trait that God hates." The man said: "O ʿAbd Allāh, what is this trait in him that God loves, and the trait in you that God hates?" He said to him: "Perhaps when he saw you, his soul suggested to him that you are better than him, and perhaps when you saw him, your soul suggested to you that you are better than him."

And it has preceded at the end of the second station in the argument of Muʿāwiyah with al-Miswar, when he said to him: "O Miswar, do you not have sins that you fear God will hold you accountable for?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And what makes you more deserving of hoping for forgiveness than me, while I and you are upon a religion in which God accepts good deeds?" — to the end of the story, until al-Miswar said: "And I knew that he was..." and thereafter he never mentioned him except with good.

And in the revealed books: "The truthful ones are warned that if I place My justice upon them, I would torment them."

And on the authority of Ḥafṣ ibn Ḥumayd, he said: "I said to Ibn al-Mubārak: 'I saw a man kill a man, and it occurred to my soul that I am better than him.' Ibn al-Mubārak said to me: 'Your fear for yourself is more severe. Look — if he is a God-fearing person who avoids polytheism, it is likely that he will be forgiven. So how can you not leave him alone, you who are certain that your opponent (1) — from his sin?' End quote. 'That if he is scrutinized in the reckoning, he will be tormented — for it is established that whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be tormented.' And the Qur'an confirms this for you: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ»} [al-Nisāʾ 4:48]. End quote.

The discourse returns to the Master of Mankind, may God bless him and grant him peace: "I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself." So how about one below him? It is fitting that whoever sees the divine favor (al-minnah) and is certain of his own shortcoming should produce the state that is its fruit — and that is the shyness that is true shyness (al-istiyāʾ ḥaqq al-ḥayāʾ).

This is the state of the man whom al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, may God be pleased with him, envied. It was said to him: "There is a man here whom we have never seen except sitting alone behind a pillar." Al-Ḥasan said: "When you see him, inform me." They looked for him one day and said to al-Ḥasan: "This is the man we told you about." So al-Ḥasan walked to him and said: "O servant of God, what prevents you from sitting with people?" He said: "A matter that has occupied me from people." He said: "And what prevents you from coming to this man called al-Ḥasan and sitting with him?" He said: "A matter that has occupied me from al-Ḥasan and from people." Al-Ḥasan said: "And what is that occupation, may God have mercy on you?" He said: "I wake and sleep between a sin and a blessing, so I saw fit to occupy myself with seeking forgiveness for my sin and gratitude for my Lord's blessing." Al-Ḥasan said to him: "O servant of God, you are more discerning (afqah) in my view than al-Ḥasan — so adhere to what you are upon." End quote.

There is no doubt that this is the reality of shyness — there remains for him no craving for a portion (ḥaẓẓ) nor any remaining with the self (baqāʾ maʿa nafs).

Tāj al-Dīn said in his Aphorisms (Ḥikam): "The aspiration of the knowers (ʿārifūn) from God is truthfulness in servitude (ṣidq bi al-ʿubūdiyyah) and the fulfillment of the right of Lordship (qiyām bi ḥaqq al-rubūbiyyah)." His commentator said: "Without seeking a portion nor remaining with the self."

And this clarifies the truth of the saying of Ibn al-ʿArabī in his Sirāj: "Al-Ṭurṭūshī used to say to us: 'Shall we go out with ourselves and devote ourselves (nabtabil) to our Lord?'" Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "I used to say to him: 'When I attain what I hope of knowledge, I will be your companion in this purpose.' And what became clear to me is that our shaykh Abū Bakr, may God be pleased with him, did not have firm resolve for this matter — for whoever desires it has no need in it for a companion except the One to whom he devotes himself." End quote, his text, may God have mercy on him. And consider — this is witnessed by what he related in al-Risālah from one of the shaykhs, who said: "I was in the desert alone, and my chest became constricted. I said: 'O jinn, speak to me! O mankind, speak to me!' A caller (hātif) said: 'What do you want?' I said: 'I want God.' The caller said to him: 'Until you want God.'" End quote.

And it is clear that all these are portions and remnants with the souls. And whoever is shy of God with true shyness — the caller cries out to him, and he is absent from all others (ghāba ʿan al-aghyār).

And one thing recalls another. He related in al-Risālah also from one of them that it was said to him: "Pray for me." He said: "It is enough for you that you make between you and your Master a mediator (wāsiṭah)." And Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: "O son of Adam, when you wish to enter upon your Master without permission, you enter upon Him." It was said: "How is that?" He said: "You perfect your ablution and enter your prayer niche — and behold, you have entered upon your Master without permission and spoken to Him without an interpreter."

And al-Ājurrī transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih: "A monk secluded himself in his hermitage in the time of Jesus, peace be upon him. Iblīs desired him but could not overcome him. Then he came to him with every visitor and said: 'Open — for if I go, you will regret it.' But he could not overcome him. Then he came to him disguised as the Messiah, son of Mary, and called out: 'O monk, look upon me so I may speak to you.' He said: 'Go to your business — I will not return what has passed of my life.' He said: 'Look upon me, for I am the Messiah.' He said: 'Even if you are the Messiah, I have no need of you. Has He not commanded us to worship and promised us the Resurrection? If you came to me today with other than that, I would not accept it from you. Go, God be with your business — I have no need of you.' So the accursed one went and left him."

They say — may God be pleased with them all — that all others (al-aghyār), lights (al-anwār), states (al-aḥwāl), this world and the next, outward and inward blessings — one should not observe any of that, nor lean upon it, nor rely upon it, whether it remains or goes. For that is a defect in the sincerity (ikhlāṣ) of one's monotheism (tawḥīd).

And in al-Ishārāt: "Do not lean upon anything other than Us. If you take refuge in works, We return them to you. If you trust in the state, We stop you with it. If you find intimacy in ecstasy (wajd), We lure you into it. If you observe creation, We entrust you to them. If you take pride in knowledge (maʿrifah), We deny it to you. So what stratagem do you have, and what strength is with you? Be pleased with Us as a Lord, until We are pleased with you as a servant."

And ʿIyāḍ transmitted in his Madārik from Ibn al-Mubārak, who said: "I passed by a weaver, and the strap of my sandal had broken. He met me with a strap (qibāl). I said: 'Did you do this for reward?' He said: 'Yes.' So whenever I passed by him, I inclined to him and greeted him. Then I missed him and found he had closed his shop. I asked some of his neighbors about him, saying: 'If he is sick, we visit him; if busy, we help him; if poor, we assist him.' They said: 'We have no knowledge of him.' So I deduced his house and he came out to me. I asked him: 'What occupied you from your shop?' He said to me: 'You, O Ibn al-Mubārak — people see you incline to me, so you clothed me in a shirt of which I have nothing. So I took its sleeve and walked with it to the graveyards, saying: "This is the grave of so-and-so, whose affair was such-and-such; and this is the grave of so-and-so, whose affair was such-and-such."' He said: 'O Ibn al-Mubārak, I do not know what you say. Not every man is the man whom tongues describe, and not every man is the man whom eyes glance at. Rather, the man is he whom God veiled in his life, then admitted him to his grave veiled, then brought him forth on the Day of Resurrection with no humiliation of disobedience upon him — that is the man.'"

And he said in al-Risālah: "And among them — meaning among the shaykhs of the Sufis — is Ruwaym ibn Aḥmad, may God have mercy on him, one of the great shaykhs. A man asked him, saying: 'Advise me.' He said: 'This matter is nothing but the expenditure of the soul (badhl al-rūḥ). If you can enter into this, then do so; otherwise, do not occupy yourself with the nonsense (tarahāt) of the Sufis.'" End quote.

And God, glorified and exalted, has said: {«وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ»} [al-Dhāriyāt 51:56]. And worship is the expenditure of utmost effort (badhl al-majhūd) in seeking the pleasure of the Worshipped One, without seeking a portion nor remaining with the self.

Tāj al-Dīn said in his Aphorisms: "How do you seek recompense for a work that is itself a gift bestowed upon you? Or how do you seek reward for a truthfulness that is itself a divine gift conveyed to you?" Al-Wāsiṭī said: "Demanding recompense for acts of obedience is a forgetfulness of divine favor (nisyān al-faḍl)."

And Tāj al-Dīn also said in his Aphorisms: "The believer is occupied by praise of God from being grateful for himself, and the rights of God occupy him from remembering his own portions."

And he also said in his Aphorisms: "Were it not for His beautiful veiling (jamil sitrihi), no work would be worthy of acceptance."

And he also said in his Aphorisms: "You are more in need of His forbearance (ḥilm) when you obey Him than you are of His forbearance when you disobey Him."

The Truthful and Confirmed One, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "None of you will enter Paradise by his works." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God envelops me with mercy from Him." (1) And in the Ṣaḥīḥ, he said: "I am the most fearful of God among you." God, mighty and majestic, said: {«إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ»} [Fāṭir 35:28].

He said in al-Iḥyāʾ: "If you are among those who stand guard (murābiṭīn) over themselves, observing themselves, you must review the states of the men and women among the worshippers, so that your zeal is stirred and your eagerness is abundant. And beware of looking at the people of your own time, for if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray. And among the best treatments of the soul is the companionship of one who strives earnestly in worship."

One of them said: "Whenever a period of languor (fatrah) befell me, I would take a single look and work upon it for a week" — looking at Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ and his striving. And indeed our Imām Mālik used to come to Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir. And Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Yaḥyā ibn Muʿīn used to frequent Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, though he was not in their rank in outward knowledge. And Imām al-Shāfiʿī used to sit before Shaybān al-Rāʿī as a boy sits in a school.

He said in al-Iḥyāʾ: "But this has become difficult, so one should return to hearing their states and reviewing their reports and what they endured of severe exertion (al-juhd al-jahīd). Their toil has ended, and their reward and bliss remain."

A group entered to visit ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and among them was a young man of emaciated body. ʿUmar said to him: "O young man, what has brought you to what I see?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, ailments and diseases." He said: "I ask you by God — but you must tell me the truth." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I tasted the sweetness of this world and found it bitter. So its bloom and freshness became small in my eyes, and its gold and its stone became equal to me. And it is as though I am looking at..."
